name: Bad Bunny
label: Rimas Entertainment
lede: He bagged groceries in Vega Baja, posted one song to SoundCloud, and in February 2026 played the Super Bowl halftime show mostly in Spanish, behind an album Pitchfork ranked No. 5 of 2025.

eras.title: The kid in the bunny ears
eras.text: Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio grew up in Almirante Sur, a barrio of Vega Baja, sang in a church choir, and bagged groceries while a scowling childhood photo waited to become a stage name.

years.h: Benito Martínez Ocasio is born in Bayamón and raised in Vega Baja
years.p: His father drove a truck, his mother taught school, and at five he was handed a Vico C album. It was his first musical memory.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, he grew up in the Almirante Sur barrio with two younger brothers and sang in his church choir until he was 13. He started writing his own songs around 14.

q: It's not about being a bad person. It's just a name that stuck.
years.h: The Easter bunny costume he hated becomes his name
years.p: At six, Benito wore a bunny costume to a school celebration and scowled his way through it. The photo of him glaring under the ears is where "Bad Bunny" comes from.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says he later figured the name would "market well." Yahoo's account has him uploading tracks to SoundCloud under it while studying audiovisual communications at the University of Puerto Rico at Arecibo and working as a grocery bagger. Wikipedia lists the job as bagger and cashier at an Econo supermarket.

He has said he briefly considered a mask, in the mold of anonymous electronic acts, then decided against hiding.

eras.title: One SoundCloud upload, one signing
eras.text: A song posted from a supermarket job reaches DJ Luian, and within two years the bagger is on Billboard's Latin chart. Latin trap is the sound; Hear This Music is the door.

years.h: DJ Luian hears "Diles" on SoundCloud and signs the bagger
years.p: Bad Bunny posts the track from a Vega Baja checkout job, and Luian puts him on his label, Hear This Music.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the solo SoundCloud release to January 25, 2016, while Bad Bunny was bagging groceries in Vega Baja. A remix with Ozuna, Farruko, [[Arcángel|47e7833f-f1a7-4703-942d-9acf12f39a1d]] and Ñengo Flow followed on August 26, 2016, produced by Mambo Kingz, DJ Luian and La Paciencia.

The remix's lyric video passed one billion YouTube views by 2023, with no official music video ever made.

years.h: His first solo single, "Soy Peor", reaches No. 19 on Hot Latin Songs
years.p: A remix with [[J Balvin|5bdeb32d-56a5-4b6d-a768-264101fa0a0a]], [[Ozuna|f2651b63-a44d-4d1d-ba64-d981d971ecd1]] and Arcángel follows in 2017, and the song eventually goes 11x Platinum (Latin) in the U.S.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Bad Bunny and DJ Luian on production and says the song made him the forerunner of Latin trap in the Latin American market.

years.cap: Bad Bunny on stage in Ecuador
years.h: Karol G brings him a top-10 Latin hit with "Ahora Me Llama"
years.p: It climbs to No. 10 on Hot Latin Songs, his first hit with a partner, and NPR's Alt.Latino names it one of the year's best Latin songs.

eras.title: Everybody wants a piece
eras.text: A Cardi B hook, a Drake feature and a surprise Christmas Eve album make a Puerto Rican trap artist a global name. In 2019 he also takes a side in a political crisis at home.

years.h: "I Like It" puts him on top of the Hot 100
years.p: Cardi B raps in English, Bad Bunny and J Balvin trade Spanish verses, and it becomes his first No. 1 in the U.S.
years.xp: Wikipedia has the single arriving in May 2018 and reaching the top of the Hot 100 that summer.

years.h: Drake joins him on "Mía" and lands a No. 5 hit
years.p: Released October 11, 2018, it is a Bad Bunny single with Drake as the guest, and it peaks at No. 5 on the Hot 100.

years.h: X 100pre arrives at midnight on Christmas Eve
years.p: He announces it the night before on social media. [[Ricky Martin|70ea63ea-70dc-4b63-951a-2c249d2b3b0a]] sings backing vocals on "Caro", [[Diplo|a56bd8f9-8ef8-4d63-89a4-794ed1360dd2]] and [[Tainy|7e92584c-ca97-48bf-8a12-0327db0f6ac8]] appear, and it peaks at No. 11 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: The title is short for "por siempre." Pitchfork gave it 8.2, Metacritic has it at 84, and Rolling Stone later ranked it No. 41 on its list of the 100 best debut albums.

years.cap: Bad Bunny in Los Angeles, October 2019
years.h: Oasis puts Bad Bunny and J Balvin on one eight-song record
years.p: It reaches No. 9 on the Billboard 200 and tops the U.S. Latin Albums chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Oasis as an eight-song album, released June 28, 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: Afilando Los Cuchillos · Wikipedia: Bad Bunny
yt: "Afilando los Cuchillos" (Residente ft. iLe & Bad Bunny)
years.h: Bad Bunny joins Residente and iLe against Governor Rosselló
years.p: "Afilando los Cuchillos" is written and recorded in a day, a response to the Telegramgate scandal. Bad Bunny also joins the protests at the Capitol demanding Ricardo Rosselló resign.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the trio went by "Residents de calle," the track pulled 2.5 million YouTube views in 24 hours, and NPR called it a clear example of a Latin American protest song. Wikipedia puts more than 500,000 Puerto Ricans at the protests, shutting down a major highway, with [[Ricky Martin|70ea63ea-70dc-4b63-951a-2c249d2b3b0a]] among the people at the Capitol.

Bad Bunny's verse hits the government for policing petty crime while underfunding schools.

eras.title: I do what I want
eras.text: The world locks down, and he fits in a Super Bowl guest slot, two albums, a concert on a flatbed truck through New York and a spot as the most streamed artist on Spotify. Then comes WWE.

years.cap: Bad Bunny and Tommy Torres performing "Amorfoda"
years.h: YHLQMDLG means "I do what I want", and it comes out on leap day
years.p: It debuts at No. 2, the highest an all-Spanish album had gone, and all 11 tracks chart on the Hot 100 at once.
years.xp: He announced it on The Tonight Show on February 27, 2020. Pitchfork scored it 8.5, calling it a party record that pays tribute to reggaeton's past and future, and the album won the Grammy for Best Latin Pop or Urban Album in 2021. It was also Spotify's most-streamed album of 2020, with 3.3 billion streams.

years.h: In the "Yo Perreo Sola" video, he performs in drag
years.p: The song tops Billboard's Latin Airplay chart, and the title makes dancing alone the point.

years.h: A flatbed dressed as a subway car carries him through New York
years.p: Bad Bunny plays a surprise concert on top of it, streamed live, and finishes at Harlem Hospital Center.

years.src: Wikipedia: El Último Tour Del Mundo
years.h: El Último Tour del Mundo is the first all-Spanish No. 1
years.p: Written during quarantine across Puerto Rico, Mexico and Los Angeles, it swaps party trap for rock, emo and acoustic moods.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.7. It opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 116,000 units, and "Dakiti" with [[Jhay Cortez|2b67658e-429f-425a-adf5-345b13112fc1]] topped the Billboard Global 200. It won Best Música Urbana Album at the 2022 Grammys.

years.h: He plays "Booker T" at the Royal Rumble, then climbs into the ring
years.p: In April he wrestles his first match at WrestleMania 37, teaming with Damian Priest against The Miz and John Morrison.
years.xp: Wikipedia has him attacking The Miz and Morrison during the Rumble, holding the WWE 24/7 Championship for 28 days, and later feuding with The Judgment Day. It ends in a street fight against Priest in San Juan on May 6, 2023.

eras.title: After the beach, the rap record
eras.text: Un Verano Sin Ti spends 13 weeks at No. 1 and turns a summer of reggaeton, bachata and indie pop into a stadium tour. Then he goes quiet and returns with a 22-track rap album.

years.h: Un Verano Sin Ti becomes Spotify's most-streamed album ever
years.p: It spends 13 non-consecutive weeks at No. 1 and is the first Spanish-language album nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys.
years.xp: Pitchfork scored it 8.4 and named it Best New Music. Wikipedia reports it topped the 2022 Billboard 200 year-end chart, a first for a Spanish-language album. The cover, by Adrian Hernandez (Ugly Primo), shows a sad one-eyed heart against a beach.

years.h: The World's Hottest Tour becomes the top-grossing by a Latin artist
years.p: Starting August 5, it plays 14 American countries and, per Wikipedia, grosses $232.5 million.

years.cap: Bad Bunny at the Forbes Under 30 summit, October 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: Nadie Sabe Lo Que Va a Pasar Mañana
years.h: Nadie Sabe Lo Que Va a Pasar Mañana is a 22-track rap record
years.p: It debuts at No. 1 with 184,000 units, and all 21 eligible tracks chart on the Hot 100.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Isabella Herrera scored it 7.4, calling it a rap homecoming that is bloated but thematically focused. Guests include [[Eladio Carrión|239e3283-3b23-4606-8c3b-b5c3bd80313d]], [[Feid|eaee97f6-f2e4-414a-966c-f31a1fb4696a]] and [[Young Miko|c4442130-e7f2-40aa-bcab-b921cc45a365]]. He told Vanity Fair he was pushing toward a new mood shaped by 1970s music.
play: Nadie Sabe Lo Que Va a Pasar Mañana

eras.title: Two chairs and a coliseum
eras.text: Plena, salsa and bomba fill a love letter to Puerto Rico, and he declines to take it on tour to the mainland U.S. He plays it for the island instead, night after night.

years.src: Wikipedia: Debí Tirar Más Fotos · Rolling Stone: Bad Bunny Makes · Pitchfork Review substack
years.h: Two plastic chairs on a patch of dirt fronting a banana grove
years.p: That's the cover of DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS, which Pitchfork gave 8.8 and ranked No. 5 of 2025. Bad Bunny said it "recommits me to Puerto Rico."
years.xp:
Released January 5, 2025 on Rimas Entertainment, the 17-track album leans on plena, jíbaro, salsa and bomba over production from [[Tainy|7e92584c-ca97-48bf-8a12-0327db0f6ac8]], MAG and La Paciencia, with Los Pleneros de la Cresta, RaiNao, Chuwi, Omar Courtz and Dei V. Metacritic has it at 95, and Rolling Stone's Maya Georgi gave it five stars, hailing "a whole new peak of greatness."

"Lo Que Le Pasó a Hawaii" tackles gentrification, and "La Mudanza" closes with a promise not to leave. It debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 before climbing to No. 1 the following week.

years.h: "DtMF" turns a plena lament into a TikTok tribute
years.p: The video for the plena-and-Nintendo-style-beat song about photos not taken arrives January 23, and the clips that follow honor lost relatives.
years.xp: It debuted at No. 38 on the Hot 100, then hit No. 1 after the Super Bowl, his first solo No. 1 in the U.S., per Wikipedia. It was nominated for Record and Song of the Year at the 2026 Grammys.

years.h: A full Puerto Rican band sets up at the NPR Tiny Desk
years.p: Bad Bunny brings the plena and jíbaro sounds of the new record into the NPR office.

years.cap: Bad Bunny at Estádio da Luz, Lisbon
years.h: The world tour announcement leaves out the U.S. mainland
years.p: Twenty-three stadium dates starting in November 2025 skip the continental U.S., over concerns about immigration enforcement at shows.

years.src: Wikipedia: No Me Quiero Ir de Aquí
years.h: El Choliseo hosts about 30 nights of No Me Quiero Ir de Aquí
years.p: The first nine shows are reserved for people living in Puerto Rico. On Sundays, guests take over "Lo Que Le Pasó a Hawaii."
years.xp:
Wikipedia counts 31 sold-out shows and more than 500,000 fans, the first residency the coliseum or Puerto Rico had hosted. Guests included Residente, Rauw Alejandro, Ivy Queen, Ozuna and Nicky Jam, with [[Rubén Blades|f050673a-dfb3-4200-b057-bf78213de36c]] and [[Luis Fonsi|d68fda90-ab8d-4799-be56-317ba4ae700f]] taking Sunday turns.

Studies put the economic impact between $176.6 million and $733 million, and hotel occupancy rose 6 percent in July.

years.h: Bad Bunny is named the Super Bowl LX halftime headliner
years.p: He becomes the first solo Latino artist to headline. Donald Trump called the pick "absolutely ridiculous," per Wikipedia.

eras.title: The whole country tunes in
eras.text: The album that skipped the mainland gets the biggest stage in American entertainment, and the biggest prize at the Grammys.

years.big: Before I say thanks to God: ICE out.
q: Before I say thanks to God, I'm going to say: ICE out
years.src: Wikipedia: Bad Bunny · Wikipedia: Debí Tirar Más Fotos
yt: Bad Bunny wins Album of the Year, 2026 Grammys
years.h: DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS becomes the first all-Spanish Album of the Year
years.p: Accepting Best Música Urbana Album earlier in the night, Bad Bunny opened with that line to a standing ovation. Later he dedicated the Album of the Year award to immigrants who left home to follow their dreams.
years.xp: He won six Grammys that night, per Wikipedia. He was also the first Latino artist nominated in all three of the Grammys' big categories in the same year, with "DtMF" up for Record and Song of the Year, and artists including Billie Eilish and Jack Antonoff wore "ICE Out" pins.

years.src: Wikipedia: Super Bowl LX halftime show
yt: Bad Bunny's Apple Music Super Bowl Halftime Show
years.h: A sugarcane field, a wedding and a halftime show mostly in Spanish
years.p: Lady Gaga plays a salsa "Die with a Smile"; Ricky Martin sings "Lo Que Le Pasó a Hawaii."
years.xp:
More than 300 dancers worked the field, a casita section drew Cardi B, Karol G and Pedro Pascal, and a real couple was married on stage with Bad Bunny signing as witness. Wikipedia counts 128.2 million U.S. viewers, the fourth-most-watched halftime show.

Trump called it "absolutely terrible," and conservative groups programmed a rival All-American Halftime Show with Kid Rock, though the FCC found no violations.
